locator.text: Equation (5.26), p. 55, in the proof of Proposition 5.3

evidence: paper: \left| \partial_{x_\perp}^{\beta} \partial_z^{k} \partial_t^{l} \bigl[ q^{b} g(x_\perp/\sqrt{q},\eta) \bigr] \right| \le C_m (1+|b|)^m \|g\|_{C^m} \, q^{\,b - a/2 - Dk - l}, \qquad m = a + k + l.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has a weaker form of it. Same object and same shape of bound, but a cruder exponent and a non-explicit constant. (i) Exponent: the paper charges a/2 per transverse derivative, D = 1/2 - h per axial derivative and 1 per time derivative, giving q^{b - a/2 - Dk - l}; the Lean charges one power of q per physical derivative of any type, giving q^{b - m} with m the total order (the docstring at BaseResidual.lean:152-153 states this loss explicitly, and ActualBaseVelocityBounds.monomial_rate packages the same rate b - m on a filter). Since 0 < h < 1/2 gives 0 < D < 1/2, we have a/2 + Dk + l ≤ a + k + l = m, so for 0 < q ≤ 1 the Lean right-hand side is at least the paper's and is strictly larger whenever a or k is nonzero: the Lean bound is implied by (5.26) and not conversely. (ii) Constant: the paper's constant is explicit, C_m (1 + |b|)^m ‖g‖_{C^m}, linear in the C^m norm of the profile and polynomial in |b|; the Lean constant is a bare existential depending on f, b, the compact set and m, with no stated dependence. (iii) Domain: the Lean quantifies over a fixed compact set K with q ≤ 1 and X in Icc lo hi (comparable to the paper's fixed compact profile range 0 ≤ X ≤ X_max, 0 < q ≤ 1), and monomial_rate localizes further to a PhysicalApproach filter rather than giving a pointwise bound on the whole range. Severity is low rather than medium because the conclusion (5.25) that (5.26) is applied to allows a lump loss K_m independent of N and a constant C_{N,m} that may depend on N, so the crude loss m and the non-uniform constant still suffice: BaseResidual.finite_error_rate (BaseResidual.lean:2477) does prove a rate 2*N*h - 2 - M whose loss 2 + M is independent of N.
